structured_guide.guide_title: CARC 18 (OA / CO-18) — Duplicate Claim Resolution Guide
structured_guide.guide_subtitle: Step-by-step duplicate claim investigation, X12 Group Code OA/CO rules, RARC M86 same-day service limitations, replacement claim logic, and payer resolution workflows.

quick_answer.title: Quick Answer: 3 Critical Questions to Resolve CARC 18

questions.question: Is the transaction an unadjudicated true duplicate submission, or a legitimate distinct service performed on the same date?
questions.summary: Under official X12 standards, CARC 18 ('Exact duplicate claim/service') is designated for use with Group Code OA (Other Adjustment), except where state workers' compensation regulations require Group Code CO (Contractual Obligation). In operational practice, commercial and Medicare payers also frequently remit CARC 18 under Group Code CO. If identical billing data was submitted twice (e.g., automatic rebill during an ERA lag or interface glitch), write off or void the redundant charge internally against the primary paid claim. If a distinct service was performed (such as a repeat EKG, bilateral procedure, distinct anatomical site, or separate encounter), append appropriate qualifying modifiers (such as 76, 77, 59, XE/XP/XS/XU, or RT/LT) supported by clinical documentation and submit as an electronic replacement claim or formal redetermination.

questions.question: Was the claim intended as a corrected/replacement claim that was misfiled with Claim Frequency Code 1 instead of 7?
questions.summary: A frequent administrative cause of false duplicate denials is submitting an amended claim as an original submission (Loop 2300 CLM05-3 = '1') rather than an electronic replacement claim (CLM05-3 = '7'). Without the replacement frequency code and the original Payer Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN in Loop 2300 REF*F8), the payer's front-end intake engines identify the second submission as an unrequested duplicate original and immediately adjust it under CARC 18.

questions.question: Does Remittance Advice Remark Code M86 accompany the denial, signaling a same-or-similar frequency limitation?
questions.summary: Note that RARC M86 does not accompany every CARC 18 adjustment; standalone CARC 18 typically indicates an exact duplicate data submission. When CARC 18 is paired with RARC M86 ('Service denied because payment already made for similar procedure within same timeframe/period'), the payer is specifically enforcing a same-or-similar medical policy, global surgical package rule, or statutory frequency limit rather than flagging an identical data transmission. Resolution requires cross-referencing payer policy guidelines, verifying whether a different physician or specialty performed the care, or submitting clinical records proving medical necessity for the repeated procedure.

code_explanation.group_code_meaning: Under official X12 standards, CARC 18 is designated for use with Group Code OA (Other Adjustments), except where state workers' compensation regulations require Group Code CO (Contractual Obligations). In operational practice, commercial and Medicare payers also frequently remit CARC 18 under Group Code CO.
code_explanation.patient_billing_scope: Under official X12 standards, CARC 18 is designated for Group Code OA (Other Adjustment), except where state workers' compensation regulations require Group Code CO (Contractual Obligation). As clarified by X12 in RFI 2814, Group Code OA indicates that an adjustment occurred but does not provide clear direction on adjustment liability on its own. It cannot be assumed that an adjustment carries zero patient liability merely because it was remitted under Group Code OA or CO. Rather, determining financial responsibility requires evaluating the group code, the complete Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA), and the adjudication outcome of the original claim together with applicable payer agreements, provider participation contracts, program rules, and statutory billing requirements. At the same time, the duplicate CARC 18 adjustment alone does not establish patient responsibility or create a separate, duplicate patient billing event. If the original claim was approved and paid, patient responsibility is governed strictly by deductible, copayment, or coinsurance amounts adjudicated under Group Code PR on the original claim's Explanation of Benefits (EOB) or 835 remittance advice. If the original claim was denied or remains in process, the provider must resolve the original claim or pursue legitimate clinical appeals rather than billing the patient on the duplicate denial. Under no circumstance does an unamended duplicate claim create independent patient liability.
what_code_establishes: The payer's claims processing system identified that key claim header or line-item elements (patient identifier, date of service, procedure code, billing/rendering NPI, or place of service) match a claim or service line already received, processed, in process, or adjudicated.
An adjustment or claim rejection was applied because payer automated adjudication rules prevent duplicate disbursements for the same episode of care.
Under official X12 standards, CARC 18 is designated for use with Group Code OA except where state workers' compensation rules mandate CO; in practice, healthcare payers remit under OA or CO.
The submitted service line or entire claim will not be paid under the current transaction because payment or adjudication has already been recorded under a prior Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN).
If accompanied by RARC M86, payment was previously made for a similar procedure within the applicable timeframe or global period (M86 does not accompany all CARC 18 adjustments).
what_code_does_not_establish: It does NOT establish that Group Code CO is the sole or universal group code for CARC 18; X12 designates Group Code OA as the primary standard.
It does NOT mean RARC M86 accompanies every duplicate adjustment; standalone CARC 18 reflects exact duplicate submissions, whereas M86 specifically denotes same-or-similar procedural limitations.

It does NOT establish fraudulent or improper billing intent; most duplicate adjustments arise from automated practice management system rebills, clearinghouse transmission loops, or misfiled corrected claims.

It does NOT establish that a second medically necessary procedure was not performed; legitimate repeat procedures, bilateral interventions, and multiple separate sessions frequently receive duplicate edits when required qualifying modifiers or encounter details are omitted.

It does NOT mean the claim is uncollectible if the service was clinically distinct and appropriately documented; distinct services are recoverable through electronic replacement claims with qualifying modifiers or formal redetermination appeals.

It does NOT mean a duplicate adjustment alone establishes patient responsibility, nor does it create a duplicate patient billing opportunity; determining financial responsibility requires examining the group code, complete ERA, and original claim adjudication outcome in light of applicable contracts and law (per X12 RFI 2814, Group Code OA does not determine liability on its own).
It does NOT constitute a medical necessity denial under CARC 50; CARC 18 is strictly an operational and clinical duplicate determination.

initial_records_checklist.record_type: 835 Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA) / Standard Paper Remittance (SPR)
initial_records_checklist.purpose: Identifies the exact CARC 18 code, affected line items, previous payment references, and companion remark codes such as M86 (similar procedure paid) or N519 (invalid combination of modifiers).
initial_records_checklist.where_to_find: Practice management (PM) system payment posting module or clearinghouse ERA archive.

initial_records_checklist.record_type: Original Adjudicated Claim Remittance (Primary ICN/DCN)
initial_records_checklist.purpose: Confirms the original claim number, processing date, paid amount, contractual adjustment, and patient liability assigned to the previously adjudicated claim.
initial_records_checklist.where_to_find: PM patient account payment history or payer provider portal claims inquiry.

initial_records_checklist.record_type: Submitted 837 Electronic Claim Files (Original vs Duplicate)
initial_records_checklist.purpose: Compares transmitted segments (Loop 2300 CLM05-3 for Frequency Code, Loop 2300 REF*F8 for Original PCCN/ICN, Loop 2400 SV1 for CPT/modifiers) between both submissions.
initial_records_checklist.where_to_find: Clearinghouse claim audit inspector or PM raw EDI 837 batch archive.

initial_records_checklist.record_type: Electronic 277CA Claim Acknowledgment & 999 Reports
initial_records_checklist.purpose: Verifies transmission timestamps and gateway acceptance for both the original submission and the contested claim to rule out transmission duplication.
initial_records_checklist.where_to_find: Clearinghouse portal under EDI transaction acknowledgment logs.

initial_records_checklist.record_type: Clinical Documentation / Operative Notes / Diagnostic Reports
initial_records_checklist.purpose: Provides objective clinical evidence of distinct anatomical site, separate operative session, repeat diagnostic testing, or separate patient encounter on the same calendar date.
initial_records_checklist.where_to_find: Electronic Health Record (EHR) clinical chart, physician progress notes, or procedure report repository.

initial_records_checklist.record_type: Encounter & Charge Entry Audit Trail
initial_records_checklist.purpose: Verifies whether double charge entry, dual interface posting, or scheduled automatic rebilling generated duplicate internal records.
initial_records_checklist.where_to_find: PM billing audit log and charge entry transaction history.

investigation_steps.title: Cross-Reference Prior Adjudicated Claim History and Remittance Records
investigation_steps.milestone: Locate the previously processed claim and determine its adjudication status and payment disposition.
instructions: Search the practice management system and payer provider portal for any claim for the same patient, date of service, and procedure code.

Compare the Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN) of the denied transaction against the original claim's ICN/DCN to identify whether the payer is comparing two separate claims or two identical service lines within the same claim.
Determine the payment disposition of the initial claim: was it paid in full, paid in part, denied for other reasons, or still actively processing in the payer's adjudication queue?
If the original claim was fully paid, examine whether the current claim represents an inadvertent second billing of the exact same charge.

records_or_fields.source_or_segment: EDI 835 Loop 2100 CLP07 or payer portal claim reference
records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Identifies the unique identifier of the original processed claim to link or contrast against the denied transaction.

records_or_fields.source_or_segment: EDI 835 Loop 2100 CLP02 / payment posting history
records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Confirms whether the earlier claim was paid (CLP02=1), denied (CLP02=4), or adjusted, establishing if revenue was already recognized.

investigation_steps.title: Audit Electronic 837 Claim Segments and Claim Frequency Codes
investigation_steps.milestone: Determine whether the submission was an intended replacement claim misfiled as an original.
instructions: Extract the raw EDI 837 transaction set for the denied claim from your clearinghouse or PM archive.
Inspect Loop 2300, segment CLM05-3 (Claim Frequency Type Code). Verify if the claim was billed with '1' (Original), '7' (Replacement / Corrected), or '8' (Void / Cancel).
If the submission was intended as a corrected claim to amend diagnosis, coding, or units, verify whether Loop 2300 REF*F8 (Payer Claim Control Number) was populated with the original claim's ICN.
If CLM05-3 is '1' on an amended submission, the payer's intake scrubber automatically treats the transaction as an unrequested duplicate original rather than a replacement.

records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Must be '7' for replacement/corrected claims; '1' indicates an original submission that triggers duplicate matching if previously received.
Must contain the exact payer claim control number of the original claim being replaced or adjusted.

investigation_steps.title: Clinically Evaluate for Distinct Procedural Services, Repeat Procedures, or Bilateral Care
investigation_steps.milestone: Determine whether multiple services were performed that require distinct procedural modifiers.
instructions: Review physician operative notes, procedure logs, diagnostic timestamps, and encounter documentation.

Verify whether the same CPT/HCPCS code was performed more than once on the same date of service (e.g., repeat EKG 93010 in morning and afternoon, repeat blood gas analysis, multiple lesion excisions, or bilateral injections).

Determine the appropriate qualifying modifier supported by clinical documentation: Modifier 76 (Repeat procedure by same physician), Modifier 77 (Repeat procedure by another physician), Modifier 59 (Distinct procedural service), Modifier XE (Separate encounter), Modifier XS (Separate organ/structure), Modifier XP (Separate practitioner), Modifier XU (Unusual non-overlapping service), or anatomical modifiers (RT, LT, E1-E4, FA-F9, TA-T9).
Confirm that clinical notes explicitly record distinct times, separate anatomical sites, or altered clinical status justifying the repeated service.

records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Verify presence of repeat/distinct modifiers (76, 77, 59, XE, XS, XP, XU, RT, LT) differentiating the service from the earlier charge.
Verify distinct procedural start/stop times, distinct anatomical locations, or separate clinical indications.

investigation_steps.title: Audit Clearinghouse Transmission Batches and Electronic Acknowledgment Logs
investigation_steps.milestone: Identify whether clearinghouse transmission glitches or dual practice management interfaces generated accidental duplicate transmissions.
instructions: Audit clearinghouse submission logs for the batch transmission date. Confirm whether duplicate 837 files were transmitted within minutes or hours of each other due to system retry protocols.
Examine 277CA Claim Acknowledgment reports for both transmissions. Verify whether the payer accepted both files (STC01-1 code A2) or rejected the second transmission.
Check practice management interface error queues to verify if a failed billing status caused an automated nightly rebill routine to retransmit the unadjudicated claim.

records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Confirms exact date, minute, and second of claim transmission to identify automated rebill loops.
Distinguishes front-end intake acknowledgment from downstream 835 claim adjudication.

timeline_and_dates.general_rules: Duplicate claim detection operates across multiple time horizons: immediate front-end intake matching (detecting identical submissions within 24 to 72 hours), historical claims history matching (evaluating services within the same calendar date), and global period matching (evaluating same-or-similar procedures across 10, 30, or 90-day post-operative or DME rental windows). When resolving CO-18, providers must align their corrective action with the governing timely filing window: for Original Medicare FFS, claims and adjustments must be filed within 1 calendar year from Date of Service under 42 CFR § 424.44; for commercial payers, replacement claims and provider dispute deadlines are established by contract and payer guidelines.

timeline_events.significance_notes: Establishes the chronological reference date from which all duplicate lookback windows, global surgical periods, and timely filing deadlines are calculated.
Demonstrates timely initial submission of the primary claim, establishing the benchmark transaction in the payer's history.
Date the original claim was adjudicated and assigned a unique Payer Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN).

timeline_events.field_or_source: EDI 837 Loop 2300 BHT04 of second submission
timeline_events.significance_notes: Date the second claim was received by the payer; determines whether submission was an inadvertent rapid rebill or a delayed replacement.

timeline_events.field_or_source: EDI 835 Loop 2100 CLP / BPR16 of duplicate denial
timeline_events.significance_notes: Triggers the commercial appeal or redetermination filing window (typically 120 days for Medicare redetermination under SSA § 1869; 180 days for commercial payer dispute).

edi_distinction_notice.ack_999_vs_277ca: A 999 Functional Acknowledgment confirms syntax and electronic envelope integrity at the clearinghouse or payer EDI gateway. A 277CA Claim Acknowledgment confirms whether the claim passed front-end syntactical edits prior to adjudication. Neither transaction represents an 835 ERA claim adjudication. Front-end 277CA rejections (such as a clearinghouse duplicate batch reject) occur prior to payer adjudication and must never be confused with an adjudicated CARC 18 adjustment reported on an 835 Electronic Remittance Advice. Un-ingested 277CA rejections cannot be appealed through provider claims dispute processes; they must be corrected and retransmitted.
edi_distinction_notice.internal_pm_dates_rule: Practice management system charge entry dates, billing batch generation dates, and internal rebill queue dates must not be confused with the electronic claim transmission date or payer adjudication date. Payer duplicate edits evaluate the actual date the electronic 837 file was ingested, not internal practice software timestamps.

decision_outcomes.title: True Duplicate Submission — Identical Claim Inadvertently Re-Billed
decision_outcomes.criteria: Investigation confirms that the claim is an exact duplicate of a previously submitted claim that has already been adjudicated or is currently processing; no distinct services, separate anatomical sites, or altered codes exist.
decision_outcomes.recommended_action: Do not rebill. Verify that payment was received and posted under the original claim's ICN. Void or write off the duplicate charge in the practice management system as a contractual adjustment/duplicate posting. Disable automatic rebill loops for the patient account.
decision_outcomes.patient_billing_rules: Do not bill the patient for duplicate charges. Patient liability cannot be established from CARC 18 or Group Code OA/CO alone (per X12 RFI 2814, OA does not determine adjustment liability on its own); any patient financial responsibility must derive exclusively from legitimate Group Code PR cost-sharing amounts assigned on the original adjudicated claim's ERA/EOB under applicable plan terms and provider contracts.

decision_outcomes.title: Legitimate Distinct Procedural Service or Repeat Procedure on Same Date
decision_outcomes.criteria: Investigation and clinical records confirm that a distinct procedure, repeat diagnostic test, separate operative session, or bilateral service was performed on the same calendar date, but submitted without qualifying modifiers or distinct clinical indicators.
decision_outcomes.recommended_action: Submit an electronic replacement claim (Claim Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 referencing the original Claim Control Number in Loop 2300 REF*F8) with the appropriate modifier (such as 76 for repeat procedure by same physician, 77 by another physician, 59 for distinct procedural service, or XE/XP/XS/XU / RT/LT). If payer rules do not permit electronic replacement for duplicate disputes, submit a formal redetermination appeal with clinical documentation, operative notes, and time-stamped diagnostic reports proving separate services.
decision_outcomes.patient_billing_rules: Do not bill the patient while the claim is under replacement or appeal. Patient billing is only permissible after the payer re-adjudicates the distinct service and assigns patient responsibility under Group Code PR.

decision_outcomes.title: Corrected Claim Misfiled as an Original Submission (Frequency Code 1)
decision_outcomes.criteria: The provider intended to submit a corrected claim to amend diagnoses, billing codes, or line items, but the transaction was transmitted with Claim Frequency Code 1 instead of Frequency Code 7, causing the payer's intake engine to reject it as a duplicate original.
decision_outcomes.recommended_action: Generate a compliant electronic replacement claim with Claim Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 and populate Loop 2300 REF*F8 with the original Payer Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN). Ensure the practice management system transmits the replacement claim file through the clearinghouse to overwrite the previous record.
decision_outcomes.patient_billing_rules: Do not bill the patient. The duplicate denial is an electronic routing defect that must be resolved through compliant replacement claim submission.

decision_outcomes.title: Same or Similar Service Frequency Limitation (RARC M86)
decision_outcomes.criteria: The claim was denied under CARC 18 paired with RARC M86 because payment was already made for a similar procedure within the same timeframe, global surgical period, or statutory frequency limit.
decision_outcomes.recommended_action: Cross-reference the procedure against payer global surgery and frequency rules. If care was rendered during a global surgical period for an unrelated condition or distinct post-operative complication, append Modifier 24 (Unrelated E/M), Modifier 78 (Unplanned return to OR), or Modifier 79 (Unrelated procedure during post-op) with supporting records. If the service was rendered by an unrelated provider or practice, file an appeal documenting independent medical necessity.
decision_outcomes.patient_billing_rules: Under Group Code CO, in-network providers cannot bill the patient unless a valid advance written beneficiary notice (such as a properly executed Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage [ABN] for Medicare FFS or a signed non-covered service agreement complying with applicable contract and balance-billing rules) was obtained prior to rendering the service.

detailed_scenarios.title: Automated Batch Rebill During Clearinghouse / Payer Remittance Lag
detailed_scenarios.trigger_condition: CARC 18 adjustment received on a secondary submission sent because the original claim appeared unpaid in the PM aging report beyond 30 days.
resolution_path: Access the payer's provider portal and perform an electronic claim search using the patient's member ID and Date of Service.
Verify whether the original claim was already processed and paid, pending in final adjudication, or denied for a different root cause.

If the original claim is paid: Locate the original 835 ERA in your clearinghouse archive. Post the primary remittance to clear the open balance on the patient account. Void or adjust off the second duplicate charge in the PM system.
If the original claim is still pending: Do not transmit additional claims. Document the original ICN and set a follow-up task based on the payer's standard adjudication turnaround.
Adjust automated billing rules in your practice management system to prevent automated rebilling of claims that have already been accepted at the clearinghouse level (STC01-1 code A2 on 277CA).
evidence_package: Original 835 Remittance Advice or portal payment voucher showing original ICN and paid amount.
Electronic 277CA Claim Acknowledgment verifying acceptance of initial transmission.
Internal PM billing audit log documenting cancellation of the redundant charge.
pitfalls_and_warnings: Do not repeatedly rebill claims simply because an 835 remittance has not arrived; rapid automated rebills trigger duplicate edits and can trigger payer pre-payment audits.
Do not file an appeal for an identical duplicate claim; an appeal cannot generate a second payment for an identical single encounter.

detailed_scenarios.title: Repeat Diagnostic Test or Treatment on Same Calendar Day (e.g., Repeat EKG / Lab)
detailed_scenarios.trigger_condition: CARC 18 or CARC 18 paired with RARC M86 received on a second diagnostic test (such as EKG CPT 93010, chest x-ray, or arterial blood gas) performed on the same date as an initial test.
resolution_path: Review medical records to confirm that two separate diagnostic tests were medically indicated and performed at distinct times on the same calendar date.
Verify whether the repeat test was performed by the same physician or a different physician within the group practice.
If performed by the same physician: Append Modifier 76 (Repeat procedure or service by same physician or other qualified health care professional) to the second CPT code.
If performed by a different physician in the same group/specialty: Append Modifier 77 (Repeat procedure by another physician or other qualified health care professional).
Submit an electronic replacement claim (Claim Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 with original ICN in Loop 2300 REF*F8).

If the payer denies the replacement claim under duplicate logic, submit a redetermination appeal with time-stamped diagnostic reports, physician orders, and clinical progress notes documenting the change in patient condition justifying the repeat testing.
evidence_package: Physician order documenting clinical indication for repeating the test.
Time-stamped initial diagnostic tracing/report and time-stamped second diagnostic tracing/report.
Clinical progress notes describing acute symptom change or treatment response between tests.
Corrected claim record with Modifier 76 or 77.
pitfalls_and_warnings: Do not append Modifier 59 when Modifier 76 or 77 accurately describes a repeat identical procedure; CPT coding conventions require repeat modifiers for identical services.
Do not submit repeat claims without explicit timestamps on both procedure reports; payers will reject un-timed repeat diagnostic tests as duplicates.

detailed_scenarios.title: Distinct Procedural Service / Separate Anatomical Site (Modifier 59 / X{EPSU})
detailed_scenarios.trigger_condition: CARC 18 received on a surgical procedure, excision, injection, or biopsy code billed multiple times on the same date of service for different anatomical locations.
resolution_path: Audit the operative report and procedure note to verify that separate lesions, distinct anatomical sites, or separate surgical incisions were involved.

Verify whether specific anatomical modifiers apply: RT (Right side), LT (Left side), E1-E4 (Eyelids), FA-F9 (Digits of hand), TA-T9 (Digits of foot). Always prefer specific anatomical modifiers over non-specific modifiers.

If anatomical modifiers are inapplicable but the service meets distinct procedural criteria, append Modifier 59 (Distinct procedural service) or the appropriate CMS subset modifier: XE (Separate encounter), XS (Separate structure/organ), XP (Separate practitioner), or XU (Unusual non-overlapping service).
Submit an electronic replacement claim (Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 and original ICN in Loop 2300 REF*F8).

If the payer requires paper appeal with clinical records for multiple surgical excisions, submit the complete operative report with all anatomical sites, pathology reports, and lesion measurements clearly highlighted.
evidence_package: Complete operative report detailing separate anatomical preparation, distinct incisions, and individual surgical sites.
Pathology reports correlating with each distinct tissue specimen.
Itemized claim showing specific anatomical modifiers (RT/LT, digits) or X{EPSU} modifiers.
pitfalls_and_warnings: Do not append Modifier 59 solely to bypass a duplicate or bundling edit without distinct clinical documentation proving separate anatomical sites or encounters.
Do not append Modifier 59 to an E/M service; use Modifier 25 for significant, separately identifiable evaluation and management services.

detailed_scenarios.title: Replacement Claim Mistakenly Submitted as Original Claim (Frequency Code 1)
detailed_scenarios.trigger_condition: CARC 18 received on an amended claim where the provider updated diagnosis codes or appended missing modifiers, but the claim was rejected in full as a duplicate.
resolution_path: Inspect the raw 837 data file for the rejected amended claim in Loop 2300 CLM05-3. Confirm that the frequency code was transmitted as '1' (Original) instead of '7' (Replacement).
Check Loop 2300 REF*F8 to determine whether the original Payer Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN) was omitted.
Correct the claim frequency code in your practice management system to '7' (Replacement / Corrected Claim).
Enter the exact original Claim Control Number from the original 835 remittance advice into the original claim reference field (populating Loop 2300 REF*F8).
Re-transmit the electronic claim to the clearinghouse. Verify on the subsequent 277CA that the claim was accepted as a replacement/adjustment transaction.
evidence_package: Original 835 ERA showing original Payer Claim Control Number.
EDI 837 claim data extract showing Loop 2300 CLM05-3 = '7' and REF*F8 populated.
Electronic 277CA acknowledgment showing acceptance of replacement claim.
pitfalls_and_warnings: Do not submit a void claim (Frequency Code 8) unless you intend to completely cancel the billing without a replacement; submitting a void without a simultaneous replacement can cause timely filing forfeiture.
Ensure the original ICN is typed exactly as formatted on the payer's remittance advice, including any required hyphens or prefixes.

detailed_scenarios.title: Multiple Providers in Same Group Practice Billing Same-Day Care
detailed_scenarios.trigger_condition: CARC 18 received when two physicians in the same multi-specialty or group practice billed services for the same patient on the same calendar date under the same Tax ID.
resolution_path: Audit the 837 claim files for both encounters. Confirm that each claim reported the distinct rendering provider's individual NPI in Loop 2310B (Rendering Provider) and distinct primary taxonomy codes in PRV03.
Determine whether the two physicians possess different medical specialties (e.g., Cardiologist seeing patient in morning for chest pain, and Orthopedic Surgeon evaluating fracture in afternoon).

If services were separate E/M encounters: Verify whether payer rules permit two same-day E/M visits; if distinct specialties, append Modifier 25 to the second visit or submit with clinical documentation demonstrating non-overlapping clinical focus.

If payer adjudication logic grouped the claims under the group Tax ID and treated the second as a duplicate: File a provider dispute or redetermination appeal enclosing both physicians' clinical progress notes, credentials, and specialty registrations proving non-duplicative care.
evidence_package: Clinical progress notes from both rendering providers establishing distinct clinical evaluations and separate times of day.
NPPES NPI registration or credentialing profiles verifying different medical specialties.
Both claim transaction extracts showing distinct rendering NPIs in Loop 2310B.
pitfalls_and_warnings: Do not bill two routine E/M visits for the same specialty on the same date without combining documentation into a single consolidated code reflecting total cumulative time or medical complexity, as CMS guidelines treat physicians of the same specialty in the same group as a single entity.
Ensure both rendering NPIs are individually enrolled with the payer under the group Tax ID.

medicare_ffs_rules.filing_deadline_rule: Under 42 CFR § 424.44, Original Medicare Fee-for-Service claims must be filed within 1 calendar year (12 months) from the Date of Service. When resolving a CARC 18 duplicate denial, any corrected or replacement claim must be submitted within this statutory 1 calendar year window. If filing a formal redetermination appeal to dispute an erroneous duplicate denial on an adjudicated claim, the appeal must be filed within 120 calendar days from the date of receipt of the initial 835 remittance advice under Social Security Act § 1869.
medicare_ffs_rules.date_convention_details: For institutional claims (Part A) involving an episode of care spanning multiple days, the timely filing limit is calculated from the 'Through' date of service under CMS IOM Pub. 100-04, Ch. 1, § 70. For professional services (Part B), the limit is calculated from the specific Date of Service of each individual line item.
medicare_ffs_rules.distinction_from_medicare_advantage: Original Medicare FFS enforces duplicate claim logic through Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) Common Working File (CWF) and Fiscal Intermediary Shared System (FISS) / Multi-Carrier System (MCS) duplicate edits governed by CMS IOM Pub. 100-04, Chapter 1, Section 120. Medicare Advantage (Part C) plans operate proprietary automated claim scrubbers and commercial claims editing engines (such as McKesson ClaimCheck or Optum CES); MA plans frequently enforce stricter same-or-similar and multiple-procedure bundling logic that requires plan-specific reconsiderations within 60 calendar days.
medicare_ffs_rules.appeal_rights_limitation: A CARC 18 adjustment reported on an adjudicated 835 remittance advice represents an initial determination under Social Security Act § 1869, affording standard 5-level Medicare appeal rights (beginning with Level 1 Redetermination by the MAC within 120 days). However, true duplicates (identical claims rebilled without alteration) have no legitimate basis for appeal and will be dismissed or reaffirmed. By contrast, claims returned as unprocessable under CMS IOM Pub. 100-04, Ch. 1, § 80 (bearing RARC MA130) lack an initial determination and carry no appeal rights; unprocessable claims must be corrected and resubmitted clean within the statutory 1-year filing limit.
medicare_ffs_rules.beneficiary_billing_restriction: Under Medicare statutory assignment agreements (Social Security Act § 1842(b)(3)(B)(ii)) and Medicare participating provider contracts, providers are strictly prohibited from billing Medicare beneficiaries for services adjusted under Group Code CO with CARC 18. Beneficiaries are not financially responsible for duplicate claims. The provider cannot convert a duplicate denial into a patient obligation unless a valid Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (Form CMS-R-131) was executed prior to the service for a known frequency or same-or-similar non-coverage limitation.

exceptions.name: Administrative Error by CMS or its Contractors (§ 424.44(b)(1))
exceptions.qualifying_conditions: Failure to timely submit or resolve a duplicate claim resulted from an error, misdirection, or delay by CMS, a Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC), or other agent of HHS performing Medicare functions.
documentation_required: Written correspondence or official logs from CMS or the MAC acknowledging system error, processing delay, or erroneous guidance.
Clearinghouse transmission logs proving timely initial delivery prior to contractor system drop.
Detailed timeline tracking the contractor's erroneous duplicate processing.

exceptions.name: Retroactive Medicare Entitlement (§ 424.44(b)(2))
exceptions.qualifying_conditions: The beneficiary received retroactive Medicare entitlement from the Social Security Administration, and the provider was unaware of coverage during the initial billing period.
documentation_required: Official SSA award letter documenting retroactive entitlement effective date.
Documentation showing initial billing to another payer or patient prior to notification.
Clean claim submitted within 6 calendar months following the month of official entitlement notice.

exceptions.name: Retroactive Medicare Entitlement Involving State Medicaid Agency (§ 424.44(b)(3))
exceptions.qualifying_conditions: A state Medicaid agency recouped payment from a provider due to retroactive Medicare entitlement, requiring Medicare billing outside normal filing limits.
documentation_required: State Medicaid recoupment notice or remittance showing reversal of payment.
Proof of original timely submission to Medicaid.
Claim submitted to Medicare within 6 calendar months of the Medicaid recoupment date.

exceptions.name: Retroactive Disenrollment from Medicare Advantage (§ 424.44(b)(4))
exceptions.qualifying_conditions: A beneficiary was retroactively disenrolled from a Medicare Advantage plan and restored to Original Medicare FFS, requiring FFS billing after MA claim processing.
documentation_required: Medicare Advantage plan disenrollment letter or recoupment remittance.
Proof of timely initial claim submission to the Medicare Advantage plan.
Clean claim submitted to the MAC within 6 calendar months following the MA recoupment or notice.

commercial_payer_rules.general_principles: Commercial health plans enforce duplicate claim controls through front-end clearinghouse intake filters, automated claim scrubbers, and core claims adjudication engines. Resolution paths depend strictly on the submission facts: if the duplicate denial was triggered by an accidental rebill or duplicate interface feed, verify payment of the original claim and void the redundant charge. If the submission was intended as a corrected claim, transmit an electronic replacement claim with Claim Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 referencing the original Claim Control Number in Loop 2300 REF*F8. If distinct services were performed on the same date, append qualifying modifiers (such as 76, 77, 59, or X{EPSU}) supported by clinical records and submit a replacement claim or formal provider dispute. Billers must adhere to the specific payer contract terms, provider manual provisions, and dispute filing deadlines.

payers.product_or_market: Commercial Managed Care (HMO, PPO, POS, Open Access Plus)
payers.timely_filing_limit: Original claim submissions: 90 calendar days from Date of Service for participating/in-network providers; 180 calendar days from Date of Service for out-of-network providers. Replacement/corrected claims: Must be submitted electronically with Claim Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 and the original Claim Control Number in Loop 2300 REF*F8; submission deadlines for corrected claims are governed by specific provider contract terms, plan provisions, or state prompt-pay regulations (do not assume the 180-day appeal limit automatically applies; verify governing contract or policy). If Cigna requests additional clinical records to substantiate distinct services, respond within the timeframe specified in the notice.
payers.secondary_claim_rule: For secondary claims, Cigna calculates timely filing from the primary payer's EOB processing date. Secondary submissions must include complete primary payment details in Loop 2320/2330.
payers.appeal_limit: Provider disputes, reconsiderations, and appeals: 180 calendar days from the date of the initial Explanation of Payment (EOP) or denial notice. For adjusted claims with subsequent payment modifications, 180 calendar days from the last payment adjustment notice.
payers.exceptions_summary: Technical transmission delays, clearinghouse batch duplicates, and concurrent multi-provider care are not automatic or guaranteed exceptions; rather, they represent extenuating circumstances that providers must document with objective submission evidence (such as clearinghouse transaction logs, provider specialty records, or operative reports) when requesting discretionary payer review or filing a dispute under applicable rules.

wrong_fix_warnings.action_to_avoid: Appending Modifier 59 indiscriminately to every duplicate denial without verifying distinct anatomical site or separate encounter documentation.
wrong_fix_warnings.why_it_fails: Modifier 59 is a designated audit trigger under the CMS National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) and commercial fraud, waste, and abuse algorithms. Unsubstantiated use of Modifier 59 to bypass duplicate edits constitutes abusive billing and can trigger pre-payment record review, post-payment recoupment, or False Claims Act exposure.
wrong_fix_warnings.correct_alternative: Review operative notes and diagnostic reports first. If a repeat identical service was performed, use Modifier 76 or 77; if distinct anatomical structures were treated, use specific anatomical modifiers (RT, LT, digits) or CMS X{EPSU} modifiers with supporting documentation.

wrong_fix_warnings.action_to_avoid: Repeatedly re-transmitting the exact same claim electronically when no payment or remittance advice is received within 30 days.
wrong_fix_warnings.why_it_fails: Automated or repeated rebilling clogs clearinghouse pipelines, generates unnecessary CARC 18 denial cycles, resets processing timers, and can lead payer claim intake systems to flag the provider's Tax ID for excessive duplicate submissions.
wrong_fix_warnings.correct_alternative: Perform an electronic 276/277 claim status inquiry or check the payer provider portal using the original claim control number. If the claim is processing, allow standard adjudication to finish; if lost, obtain clearinghouse trace logs before retransmitting as a linked replacement.

wrong_fix_warnings.action_to_avoid: Filing a formal redetermination appeal for an unamended, true duplicate charge generated by internal practice management double-posting.
wrong_fix_warnings.why_it_fails: Appeals departments cannot authorize a second payment for an identical single encounter. Submitting appeals on true duplicates wastes administrative labor and delays genuine appeals.
wrong_fix_warnings.correct_alternative: Reconcile the patient account against the primary claim's 835 ERA payment. If payment was properly applied to the original claim, void or adjust the duplicate charge internally under contractual obligation.

wrong_fix_warnings.action_to_avoid: Submitting a corrected claim as an original claim (Claim Frequency Code 1) rather than a replacement claim (Claim Frequency Code 7).
wrong_fix_warnings.why_it_fails: Payer intake systems evaluate Frequency Code 1 submissions against existing claim history as new, independent encounters. If dates, provider, and patient match an existing claim, it is automatically rejected as a duplicate original.
wrong_fix_warnings.correct_alternative: Transmit the amended claim with Claim Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 and populate Loop 2300 REF*F8 with the original Payer Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN).

prevention_controls.operational_action: Configure clearinghouse claim scrubbers to block outgoing claims that share an identical patient, Date of Service, CPT code, and billing Tax ID with a claim transmitted within the preceding 90 days, unless a qualifying distinct procedural modifier (59, 76, 77, XE, XS, XP, XU, RT, LT) or Claim Frequency Code 7 is detected.

prevention_controls.control_name: Automated Rebill Suspension & Remittance Reconciliation Protocol
prevention_controls.operational_action: Disable automated batch rebilling in practice management software. Require billing staff to verify electronic 277CA acceptance and 276/277 claim status inquiry before re-dropping any claim over 30 days old.

prevention_controls.control_name: Same-Day Procedural Coding & Modifier Review Protocol
prevention_controls.operational_action: Implement a mandatory coder review queue for any patient encounter containing multiple instances of the same CPT code or multiple provider visits on the same calendar date, ensuring clinical timestamps and anatomical modifiers are verified prior to claim generation.

final_resolution_checklist: Verify the adjudication status of the primary claim: confirm whether it was paid, denied, or is currently processing under a valid Payer Claim Control Number (ICN/DCN).
If the claim is a true duplicate, verify that payment was posted under the primary claim, and void the duplicate charge in the practice management system as a contractual adjustment.
If the claim was an intended corrected claim, verify that it was transmitted with Claim Frequency Code 7 in Loop 2300 CLM05-3 and that Loop 2300 REF*F8 contained the original ICN.
If the service was a distinct procedure or repeat test, confirm that clinical documentation, timestamps, and operative notes substantiate separate care.
Verify that the appropriate modifier (76, 77, 59, XE, XS, XP, XU, RT, LT) was appended to the distinct service line.

Ensure that no duplicate balance billing was directed to the patient, and that patient responsibility is assessed only from Group Code PR determinations on the primary claim's remittance advice in accordance with provider contracts and applicable rules (recognizing per X12 RFI 2814 that OA does not determine liability on its own).

quick_answer.title: Quick Answer: 3 Critical Questions to Resolve CO-22

questions.question: Which health plan is legally primary under statutory MSP rules or governing state/ERISA COB provisions?
questions.summary: CARC 22 indicates that the payer believes another health plan or third party holds primary financial responsibility for the claim. Payer sequencing is strictly governed by statutory criteria and plan contracts. For commercial coverage, rules follow state insurance regulations (frequently patterned on NAIC Model Regulation #120) or governing ERISA Summary Plan Descriptions (Subscriber vs. Dependent, Birthday Rule for dependent children, Active Employee vs. Retiree/COBRA). NAIC Model #120 is a model regulation subject to state adoption and ERISA terms, not a universal federal mandate. For Medicare, apply statutory Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) rules under 42 U.S.C. § 1395y(b) and 42 CFR Part 411: Medicare is secondary ONLY when specific statutory thresholds are met—Working Aged EGHP with 20+ employees, Disability LGHP with 100+ employees, during the 30-month ESRD coordination period, or for liability/no-fault/workers' compensation. If the employer has fewer than 20 employees (Working Aged) or fewer than 100 employees (Disability), or after the 30-month ESRD coordination period ends, Medicare is legally PRIMARY. Furthermore, Medicare is legally PRIMARY over commercial retiree group health coverage (as statutory MSP applies strictly to active employment status under 42 CFR § 411.170). Separately, Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plans (standardized under Social Security Act § 1882) are private supplemental policies designed exclusively to cover Medicare cost-sharing, and always pay secondary to Medicare as a supplemental payer.

questions.question: Has the primary plan already adjudicated the service, and was the primary 835 remittance data accurately transmitted in Loop 2320/2330?
questions.summary: If the billed payer is legitimately secondary, a CO-22 denial usually signals that the secondary claim was submitted without required primary payer adjudication data. Under HIPAA 837 transaction standards, secondary electronic claims must transmit complete primary claim-level adjustments (Loop 2320 CAS), primary paid amounts (Loop 2320 AMT01=D), primary payer identification (Loop 2330A NM1), and line-level adjustments (Loop 2430 SVD/CAS). Check whether companion remark codes such as RARC N4 ('Missing/incomplete/invalid prior insurance carrier EOB') or MA64 ('Prior-payer payment information is required before this claim can be processed') accompany the adjustment; note that neither remark universally accompanies CARC 22.

questions.question: Is the denial caused by stale member COB records requiring an updated coordination questionnaire?
questions.summary: Commercial payers frequently issue automated CO-22 denials on an annual basis when their records indicate a member may have dual coverage. When the payer's enrollment engine flags a missing annual COB update, the payer will freeze claim payment until the subscriber contacts the plan or completes an online COB questionnaire verifying whether other coverage exists. In these scenarios, the provider must coordinate with the patient to complete the payer's required coordination update.

code_explanation.group_code_meaning: Contractual Obligation (CO) indicates an adjustment resulting from a contract between the payer and participating provider, or an applicable fee schedule/regulatory mandate.
code_explanation.patient_billing_scope: Group Code CO (Contractual Obligation) assigned to CARC 22 reflects an adjustment where the payer asserts that another health plan or insurer holds primary responsibility. Under in-network participating provider agreements and Medicare rules, a provider cannot immediately balance-bill the patient for the unpaid balance upon receiving a CO-22 denial. The CO adjustment indicates an unresolved coordination-of-benefits workflow, not an established patient liability. Patient billing is only permissible if and when the primary or secondary payer adjudicates the claim and officially assigns patient responsibility under Group Code PR (such as deductibles, copayments, or coinsurance). If a commercial payer denies coverage because the member refuses or fails to cooperate with an annual COB questionnaire after documented provider outreach, the provider must review the governing in-network contract and state balance-billing regulations before pursuing any patient balance.
what_code_establishes: The payer's adjudication system determined that based on current enrollment records, coordination-of-benefits data, or statutory rules, another payer holds primary or prior financial responsibility for the claim.
An adjustment was applied because the claim was either submitted to the wrong payer as primary, or submitted to a secondary payer without required primary adjudication details.
Under X12 EDI standards, the transaction requires proper cross-payer coordination, complete primary remittance data, or member coordination updates before secondary benefits can be determined.
If accompanied by RARC N4 or MA64, the secondary payer specifically identifies missing prior carrier EOB or prior-payer payment details (neither remark code universally accompanies CARC 22).
what_code_does_not_establish: It does NOT establish that the patient's care is non-covered or medically unnecessary; CARC 22 is strictly a payer sequencing and coordination determination.

It does NOT establish that the provider will not be reimbursed; reimbursement is recoverable upon submitting to the proper primary payer or submitting a compliant secondary claim with Loop 2320 primary payment data.
It does NOT authorize immediate balance billing to the patient under Group Code CO; patient liability is restricted to amounts adjudicated under Group Code PR on a final Explanation of Benefits.

It does NOT constitute a final denial if conditional payment rules apply under Medicare Secondary Payer regulations (42 CFR § 411.52) for un-adjudicated liability/workers' compensation claims (conditional payments do not apply to commercial health plan disputes).

It does NOT establish that Medicare is always secondary; Medicare is statutory primary if employer size thresholds are not met (<20 employees for Working Aged, <100 employees for Disability), after the 30-month ESRD coordination period ends, when coordinating with commercial retiree group coverage (where active employment status is absent under 42 CFR § 411.170), or when coordinating with Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plans (which under SSA § 1882 are supplemental policies that always pay after Medicare).
It does NOT mean the patient was uninsured on the Date of Service; it indicates that multiple potential coverage sources require chronological alignment.

investigation_steps.title: Establish Authoritative Payer Sequencing (State COB / ERISA Rules & Medicare MSP Criteria)
investigation_steps.milestone: Determine with legal certainty which insurance plan is primary and which is secondary for the Date of Service.
instructions: Audit patient demographics and coverage profiles to identify all active insurance policies on the Date of Service.

For commercial coverage, apply governing state coordination regulations (frequently patterned on NAIC Model Regulation #120) or governing ERISA Summary Plan Descriptions: (a) Subscriber vs. Dependent: the plan covering the patient as an employee/subscriber is primary over a plan covering the patient as a dependent; (b) Dependent Children (Birthday Rule): the plan of the parent whose birthday (month and day) falls earlier in the calendar year is primary; (c) Active vs. Inactive: coverage from active employment is primary over retiree or COBRA coverage. Note that NAIC Model #120 is a model regulation subject to state adoption and ERISA plan terms, not a universal federal statute.

If Medicare is involved, apply statutory Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) rules under 42 U.S.C. § 1395y(b) and 42 CFR Part 411: (a) Working Aged: Employer Group Health Plan (EGHP) is primary if employer has 20 or more employees; if employer has fewer than 20 employees, Medicare is legally PRIMARY; (b) Disability: Large Group Health Plan (LGHP) is primary if employer has 100 or more employees; if employer has fewer than 100 employees, Medicare is legally PRIMARY; (c) End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD): EGHP is primary during the statutory 30-month coordination period, after which Medicare becomes legally PRIMARY regardless of employer size; (d) Retiree Group Health Plans: Under 42 U.S.C. § 1395y(b) and 42 CFR § 411.170, statutory MSP rules apply only to individuals with 'current employment status'. Because retiree health coverage is based on past employment, Medicare is legally PRIMARY, and the commercial retiree group health plan pays secondary according to its plan terms; (e) Medicare Supplement (Medigap) Policies: Governed under Social Security Act § 1882 [42 U.S.C. § 1395ss], Medigap policies are standardized private health insurance products specifically designed to pay Medicare Part A and Part B patient cost-sharing (deductibles, copayments, coinsurance); Medigap is strictly a supplemental policy that always pays after Medicare and is never primary under any circumstance; (f) Workers' Comp / No-Fault / Liability: Non-Medicare insurance is primary for accident-related care under 42 U.S.C. § 1395y(b)(2).
Identify whether the claim was mistakenly billed to the secondary payer as primary, or if the primary payer has already adjudicated the claim.

records_or_fields.source_or_segment: State COB Rules / ERISA SPD / 42 U.S.C. § 1395y(b) & MSP Questionnaire
records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Identifies legal order of liability (Primary vs. Secondary vs. Tertiary) based on statutory, regulatory, and contractual criteria.
Verifies employer employee threshold (20+ for Working Aged; 100+ for Disability; <20 or <100 where Medicare is primary) to determine Medicare primary vs secondary status.

investigation_steps.title: Audit Primary Payer Adjudication and Remittance Data (Loop 2320/2330)
investigation_steps.milestone: Verify whether complete primary adjudication details were extracted and transmitted on the secondary claim.
instructions: If the primary payer has not yet processed the claim: Submit the claim immediately to the proper primary payer as an original submission.
If the primary payer has already processed the claim: Obtain the complete 835 ERA or paper Explanation of Benefits from the primary payer.

Inspect the raw 837 electronic secondary claim file to verify that primary adjudication elements were mapped into Loop 2320 and Loop 2330: (a) Loop 2320 SBR (Other Subscriber Information); (b) Loop 2320 CAS (Claim-Level Adjustments with CARC, Group Code, and dollar amount from primary EOB); (c) Loop 2320 AMT (Primary Payer Paid Amount with AMT01='D'); (d) Loop 2330A NM1 (Other Payer Name and Payer ID); (e) Loop 2430 SVD & CAS (Line-Level Primary Payment and Adjustments).
If primary data was omitted or corrupted during clearinghouse translation, correct the secondary claim mapping and resubmit electronically.

records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Must match the exact total payment disbursed by the primary payer on the primary 835 remittance.

records_or_fields.field: Primary Claim Adjustment Reason & Group Codes
records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Must mirror the exact CARC and Group Code (CO, PR, OA, PI) amounts adjudicated by the primary payer.
Must contain the valid electronic Payer ID of the primary insurance carrier.

investigation_steps.title: Investigate Member COB Questionnaire Status & Coordination Blocks
investigation_steps.milestone: Determine whether the denial is driven by an un-updated annual COB questionnaire in the payer's enrollment system.
instructions: Call the denying payer's provider services line or inspect the payer portal to check member COB status.
Ask the payer representative: 'Is this claim denied because the member has not completed their annual coordination of benefits questionnaire, or because you have active primary insurance on file?'

If the payer has an active primary policy on file: Obtain the name, policy number, and effective dates of the other insurance recorded in the payer's system. Cross-reference with patient records to verify if the policy is active or terminated.

If the member's annual COB questionnaire is outdated: Contact the patient/subscriber immediately. Instruct the patient to contact their health plan's member services number (or log into their member portal) to complete the COB update.
Offer to facilitate a three-way call between the patient, provider office, and the insurance carrier to expedite the COB record update and obtain a reference number.

records_or_fields.field: Payer Member COB Flag / Survey Status
records_or_fields.source_or_segment: Payer Provider Portal / Representative Call Log
records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Confirms whether the member's coordination status is active, expired, or locked pending questionnaire submission.

records_or_fields.field: Other Insurance Active Dates in Payer System
records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Verifies whether the alleged primary policy was active on the Date of Service or terminated prior to care.

investigation_steps.title: Evaluate Terminated Prior Coverage and Generate Proof of Termination
investigation_steps.milestone: Document coverage termination when the payer's records erroneously show inactive prior coverage as primary.
instructions: If the payer asserts another plan is primary, but the patient confirms that coverage was cancelled or terminated prior to the Date of Service: Obtain an official Certificate of Creditable Coverage (COCC) or termination letter from the prior carrier.
If a termination letter is unavailable, obtain a real-time 271 eligibility response or letter from the prior employer showing the exact termination date.
Submit the proof of termination along with a formal claim reconsideration request to the denying payer's COB / Eligibility Update department.
Request that the payer update their member coordination records and reprocess the claim as primary.

records_or_fields.what_to_verify: Demonstrates that prior coverage ended before the Date of Service, disproving primary liability.

records_or_fields.source_or_segment: Provider Written Inquiry / Portal Dispute Submission
